CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in fingers and pain in right wrist.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a landscaper presenting with several months of pain and numbness in the right wrist and hand. Symptoms began insidiously without known precipitating event. Patient reports symptoms are most noticeable at night, frequently waking with hand numbness requiring shaking out. Numbness affects all fingers but is more prominent in thumb and index finger, with occasional involvement of fifth finger. Patient denies similar symptoms in right hand. Weakness noted in left hand with difficulty gripping and dropping objects due to decreased sensation. Patient attributes heavy labor and repetitive motions from landscaping work as potential contributing factors.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports numbness and tingling in left hand fingers, particularly thumb and index finger. Weakness in left hand grip noted. Denies right hand involvement. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works in landscaping doing yard work and maintenance. Work involves repetitive heavy labor with raking and digging. Alcohol consumption consists of one to two beers on Friday and Saturday weekends.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart and lungs auscultated and normal. Grip strength decreased on left hand compared to right. Sensation intact to touch on right side fingers with slight abnormality on thumb side. Bilateral positive Tinel's sign elicited at wrist.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome. Plan includes activity modification with delegation of repetitive work tasks to employees for several weeks. Wrist splint prescribed. Ibuprofen 600 mg every six hours prescribed. Electromyography (EMG) study ordered to measure electrical impulses. Follow-up appointment scheduled in two weeks to assess response to conservative treatment and determine need for further diagnostic testing or possible surgical intervention.
